analysis.title: Tesla Inc. Company Update: Robotaxi, Optimus, and SpaceX merger
key_insights: Deutsche Bank reiterates Buy and a $420 price target on Tesla. The stock closed at $372.22 on 23 Oct 2026.

Robotaxi unsupervised miles reached 3.1m as of Oct-18, up nearly 9x in three months by DB's estimate. Cybercab entered paid service in Austin on Sep-3 and the local fleet has grown about 10x since launch.
Management targets 24/7 service, highways, higher speeds and broader weather coverage in Austin by year-end. Dallas is expected to launch next month, with more cities ramping by year-end.
FSD v15 (supervised) is slated for wide release to owners this year. It becomes unsupervised in geo-fenced areas in 2Q27, and Cybercab owners should be able to join the managed network in 2Q27.

Cybercab is targeted for consumers later this year at small volume, with the captive fleet the priority. Installed annual capacity at the Texas facility is above 125k units, and the ramp is seen as less constrained because of a ~50% cut in parts count.

Optimus expectations remain fairly low. First production-quality units are coming off the line in Fremont, and most equipment for a nominal 1m per year line is in place. Reaching 20k units per week is expected to take at least a year per management, and DB says it could take much longer.

Tesla is setting up an Optimus Academy where roughly 10-20k early units practice tasks via self-play to generate real-world data. A new demo video is expected within one to two months, AI5 chip integration is targeted for April 2027, and first external industrial deliveries are aimed at the end of 2027.

Special committees of independent directors have been formed at Tesla and SpaceX to evaluate a combination. Musk says he is conflicted and not participating, supports a deal, and cautions that terms are not agreed and there is no guarantee. Tesla approval would need a 50% vote of all outstanding shares.

DB thinks a substantial premium may be needed to secure the vote and limit legal challenge risk, assuming an all-stock deal. It sees this as likely putting a floor under the stock and making Tesla a proxy for the premium needed to pass a vote, and as the main driver of the stock going forward.
DB sees the main obstacle as how to handle Tesla's large and profitable China operations, given SpaceX is a critical supplier to the US government.

Estimate changes are mostly minor, except energy-storage pricing, which DB sees on a healthier trajectory helped by AI data center demand. 2026E revenue rises to $107,220m from $106,100m, and 2026E EPS (non-GAAP) rises to $1.66 from $1.40.

market_movers.rationale: Robotaxi progress is encouraging and energy-storage pricing is improving. A possible SpaceX merger may put a floor under the shares as a premium is needed to win the vote.

earnings_insights: Tesla 2026E non-GAAP EPS is raised to $1.66 from $1.40 (DB estimate, not a reported figure). 2027E is $1.44 vs $1.40 prior.
2026E revenue is $107,220m vs $106,100m prior (DB estimate). 2027E is $112,857m vs $110,326m.
2026E energy/storage revenue is cut to $12,497m from $13,312m, while 2027E rises to $18,283m from $17,155m (DB estimate).
2026E auto gross margin (GAAP) is raised to 18.5% from 17.9%, and ex-credit to 17.7% from 16.8%. 2027E is unchanged at 16.9% GAAP and 16.0% ex-credit (DB estimate).
2026E free cash flow is revised to -$693m from -$9,150m, and 2027E to -$14,302m from -$17,015m (DB estimate).
risk_factors: No agreement on merger terms between the Tesla and SpaceX special committees, and no guarantee of one.
A Tesla merger vote needs 50% of all outstanding shares, not just shares voted, and a premium may be needed to avoid legal challenges.
Handling Tesla's China operations given SpaceX's role as a US government supplier.
Optimus ramp could take much longer than management's at least one year to reach 20k units per week, with ~10,000 elements needing to go right.
Robotaxi expansion to 24/7 service, highways and more cities depends on FSD v15 timelines.
geopolitical: SpaceX is a critical supplier to the US government, which complicates the treatment of Tesla's large China operations in a possible merger.

tension_points.bull_case: A combination could bring gains from cooperating on superintelligence software, chip design, Terafab, robotics and Starlink, per Musk. DB thinks the premium needed to win the vote may put a floor under Tesla's share price.
tension_points.bear_case: The committees have not agreed on terms and there is no guarantee they will. China operations are a main obstacle given SpaceX's role as a critical US government supplier.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The special committees failing to agree on terms, or a deal that cannot clear the 50% vote of all outstanding shares.
